question: Can a memory network with soft attention over an external memory and multiple hops be trained end-to-end without supporting-fact supervision, on QA and language modeling?
hypothesis: Multiple computational hops over a continuous memory improve results, and removing hard max makes the model trainable by backpropagation with less supervision.
contributions: A continuous (softmax) form of Memory Network trained end-to-end from input-output pairs
Multi-hop stacking with adjacent and layer-wise weight tying
Position encoding, temporal encoding, random-noise and linear-start training tricks
Competitive results on bAbI QA and Penn Treebank/Text8 language modeling

method.summary: Each sentence (or word) is embedded into input memory vectors m_i (matrix A) and output vectors c_i (matrix C); a query embedding u attends over memories by softmax of inner products, the weighted sum o is added to u, repeated for K hops, then a final matrix W and softmax predict the answer. Trained with cross-entropy and SGD on bAbI QA and on word-level language modeling.

datasets.name: bAbI QA tasks v1.1 (20 tasks)
datasets.size: 1000 or 10,000 training problems per task; vocabulary V=177; up to 320 sentences per story
datasets.split: 10% of training set held out for validation; test as provided
datasets.preprocessing: memory limited to most recent 50 sentences; null-symbol padding with zero embedding; list answers treated as single vocabulary words

datasets.name: Text8
datasets.preprocessing: words occurring fewer than 5 times replaced by <UNK>

models.name: MemN2N
models.layers: K=3 hops default for QA; 2-7 hops for LM
models.hidden: d=20 (independent) or d=50 (joint) for QA; d=100 for RN* model; 150 (PTB) / 500 (Text8) for LM

other.weight_tying: adjacent default; layer-wise (with H matrix) for LM and LW rows
other.lm_details: query fixed to constant vector 0.1; ReLU on half of the units per layer; layer-wise sharing

models.name: MemNN (strongly supervised AM+NG+NL)
models.architecture: Memory Network with max ops, n-gram, nonlinear layers, adaptive hops

models.name: LSTM / RNN / SCRN
models.architecture: recurrent baselines (LM numbers from Mikolov et al. 2014)

training.objective: cross-entropy between predicted and true answer (QA) or next word (LM)
training.lr: 0.01 (QA), halved every 25 epochs until 100 epochs; 0.005 for linear start; joint: 60 epochs (1k) / 20 epochs (10k) with halving every 15 / 5 epochs
training.lr_schedule: QA: eta/2 every 25 epochs; LM: divide by 1.5 if validation cost has not decreased after one epoch, stop when lr < 1e-5 (~50 epochs)
training.regularisation: gradient clipping at l2 norm 40 (QA, per weight matrix) and 50 (LM, whole gradient); random-noise 10% empty memories
training.seeds: QA: 10 restarts, pick lowest training error; PTB: 10 restarts, pick lowest validation cost; Text8: single run

other.linear_start: softmax removed from memory layers until validation loss stops decreasing, then reinserted

inference.decoding: argmax of softmax over answer vocabulary
inference.retrieval: soft attention over all stored memories

metrics.name: test error rate
metrics.definition: percentage of wrong answers per bAbI task; mean over 20 tasks; failed task = error > 5%

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: test perplexity on PTB and Text8

eval.protocol: best of 10 random initialisations chosen on training error (QA) or validation cost (PTB); validation split used for architecture and hyperparameters

limits: Authors concede it does not match strongly supervised MemNN and both fail several 1k tasks.
Authors state smooth lookups may not scale well to larger memories; propose multiscale attention or hashing.
Synthetic bAbI with vocabulary of 177; language-model gain is small (111 vs 115 perplexity) and Text8 is a single run.
Best-of-10 initialisation selection uses training error on QA, so reported errors are not single-run averages.
Hardware, compute and wall-clock not stated.
